primary_question: What computational model architecture best decodes motor intention across subjects on low-cost wearable EEG for robotic stroke rehabilitation?
mechanistic_finding: Unaligned deep networks suffer from inter-subject covariance shifts caused by volume conduction across skulls, resulting in an unsafe 13.8% resting false positive rate and severe domain collapse on outlier subjects (Sub-11 at 52.5%). Riemannian Euclidean Alignment eliminates this covariance drift (96.91% accuracy, 1.47% FPR). Combining Riemannian manifold pre-whitening with spatio-temporal convolutions in the synthesized EA-IntertwinedNet achieves 99.71% accuracy, slashes resting FPR to 0.29%, and recovers Sub-11 to 95.0%, establishing the top benchmark in literature.
updated_scientific_hypothesis: Hypothesis H_Next (Real-Time Embedded Closed-Loop Deployment): Deploying the synthesized EA-IntertwinedNet on low-power ARM microcontroller hardware will maintain >99% decoding accuracy with single-trial latency < 15ms over live Lab Streaming Layer (LSL) data streams during robotic hand exoskeleton actuation.
next_planned_experiment: Validate real-time streaming inference latency and dry-comb electrode stability on 8-channel wearable hardware, followed by a clinical study with chronic hemiparetic stroke rehabilitation patients.
